added_failures_note: the reviewed run records baseline_suite as 'not run at this node' (its declared measure is the focused gate, not a suite arm) and after_suite as prose naming two green gate logs; neither arm carries the armed-only JSON shape, so no suite-derived added failures exist. The reviewed run's own gate logs are gate-staged-53loop.log (42 passed) and gate-live-27loop.log (39 passed), both reproduced independently by this reviewer at the reviewed head with zero failures, so added_failure_count is 0 and added_failure_ids is empty.

findings.reason: The landed section states 'Those eight pairs (loops 19..26) track the type-6 prediction at a slope of about -1 and a correlation below -0.9.' The test's own filter is `if difference.std() < 2 * measured_reference.std(): continue`, and the measured set is seven pairs, loops 19..25, not eight. Reproduced at review time in a scratch checkout of the reviewed head against the staged bundle: the reference excursion std is 0.290912 and the threshold is 0.581823; loop 26's measured difference std is 0.575255 (ratio 1.9774), so loop 26 is below the threshold and is dropped. The scored pairs are loops 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 and 25, with correlations -0.919, -0.940, -0.954, -0.954, -0.943, -0.939 and -0.931; all seven pass the -0.9 assertion and, with the subtraction reversed, none do. The fragment is the plan's durable evidence record, so its own stated measurement should reconcile with the gate it cites.
findings.text: correct the fragment's landed section to 'seven pairs (loops 19..25)', or state the ratio loop 26 carries (1.977 against the 2.0 threshold) if the near-miss is the point being made. Either way the count and the loop range must match what the test scores.

findings.reason: A type-6 differential SensorMapping is built at geometry_adapter.py:223 with efm_index=-1, while every positioned flux loop carries efm_index in 0..len(loops)-1. `_apply_flux_loop_position_declarations` (geometry_adapter.py:718-750) writes `updated_loops[mapping.efm_index] = FluxLoop(...)` whenever a position declaration matches a mapping's channel, and -1 is a legal list index, so a declaration naming a differential channel silently overwrites the LAST positioned loop, reporting success rather than raising. Reproduced at review time with the real function and a synthetic three-loop geometry table plus a type-6 mapping: `_apply_flux_loop_position_declarations` returned loops [(0,1.0,2.0),(1,2.0,3.0),(-1,99.0,98.0)] — the third positioned loop replaced by the declaration's coordinates and index -1 — with the notice 'flux-loop vacuum-position declarations: 1 directional coordinates applied'. It is latent, not live: only MAST carries non-empty flux_*_position_declarations in-repo, MAST has no type-6 entries, and the JT-60SA map lives in the /work bundle, so no shipped catalogue triggers it today. The operator's own use of the sentinel is guarded (it skips mappings whose indices_differential is set when keying row_of_loop), so the hazard is confined to the adapter's declaration path.
findings.text: make the not-applicable case unable to index: skip a mapping whose indices_differential is set before `updated_loops[mapping.efm_index]` is reached, or widen the type and use None as the not-applicable value, so a differential channel can never resolve to a positioned loop slot.

item_verdicts.diff: read fc8cf68d and 8d75c8c7 against bff5f22e. The adapter change adds an indices_differential role suffix, a branch that validates the pair is exactly two indices, converts DD 1-based indices to geometry-table slots, and refuses an out-of-range pair with GeometryAdapterError, and lets a differential mapping survive _sensor_map_for_acquisition with no finite coordinate. The operator change adds _apply_differential_rows, applied to g_pf, g_plasma and g_passive only after the kernel has assembled them, returning the matrices unchanged when no differential mapping is present. The tests add 324 lines: a 53-loop store rebuilt under tmp_path from the merged builder, the structural identity of all 26 differential rows against their two positioned rows in all three blocks, and the vacuum fit that scores the pairs whose measured difference exceeds twice the reference excursion. The implementation is coherent and its differential convention (second minus first, matching the DD's indices_differential) is correct throughout.
item_verdicts.done_when: the dispatched measure for this node is the two gates plus the declared negative control. gate-staged-53loop.log (42 passed) and gate-live-27loop.log (39 passed) are both reproduced by this reviewer at the reviewed head, from a scratch extraction of 8d75c8c7, against the staged and live bundles respectively: 42 passed in 173.18s and 39 passed in 114.85s, EXIT=0 both. The negative control is also reproduced independently by reversing the operator's subtraction in the scratch tree, which turns the two differential tests red (EXIT=1, the same two ids the reviewed run's negative_control_log.txt records). `ruff check imas_ambix tests` exits 0. The map and stores the staged gate needs are present in the node's staging directory and the tracked worktree carries no change to them.
item_verdicts.goal: Plan section 6's jtmm-differential-loop-consumers asks for one node that makes the machine-map adapter carry a type-6 magnetics/flux_loop entry by its indices_differential in place of a position, makes the JT-60SA map's flux-loop position bindings expand over the commit's type-1 entries only, and makes read_geometry_table and build_operator predict a type-6 entry as its second loop minus its first, with MAST unchanged. The commit does exactly that: SensorMapping gains an indices_differential tuple; a family carrying that array is carried with efm_index=-1, r=z=NaN and no geometry-table slot; the DD 1-based pair becomes 0-based slots and the operator rewrites each differential row as second_row minus first_row in g_pf, g_plasma and g_passive alike; and a geometry with no differential entry returns every matrix unchanged, which is MAST's case. The map half is the per-store split the coordinator resolved (option 1): the staged map carries 27 per-entry position bindings plus 26 per-entry indices_differential bindings and serves the 53-loop store only.
item_verdicts.manifest: the reviewed manifest reports status complete, two commits (fc8cf68d, 8d75c8c7), the six changed repo paths, both gate logs, a negative_control_log whose last line is EXIT=1 with two failing ids the head arm does not fail, and a follow_ons entry naming the promotion coupling. Its baseline_suite field reads 'not run at this node', which is honest for a focused-gate node and is why no armed suite pair exists to derive added failures from. One narration line in its checkpoint is inconsistent with the datable attempt boundaries — it says the resumed-attempt fence deadline 2026-10-07T12:25:50Z 'was passed by about five minutes' while the manifest mtime is 12:03:39Z and the attempt exited at 12:04:12Z — but the record's facts (commits, gates, negative control, scope) all reconcile against the tree and the logs.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed commits touch only declared paths. fc8cf68d changes imas_ambix/data/geometry_adapter.py, imas_ambix/gs/geometry.py, imas_ambix/gs/operator.py, tests/data/test_jt60sa_machine_map.py and tests/gs/test_operator_differential_loops.py (+425/-2); 8d75c8c7 changes only docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-machine-map/jtmm-differential-loop-consumers.html (+37/-1). imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py is declared but unchanged. The staged map and its stores are written only under the declared staging directory outside the repository. The live bundle is provably untouched: /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/machine_description/OP1/magnetics.nc still carries 27 flux_loop entries with an mtime of 2026-10-06T18:14, predating this run, and this reviewer wrote only its two fenced record paths plus its own run directory, with scratch under /tmp.

justifications.durability: the operator and adapter changes are small, well-combed and reuse the existing per-entry struct_array_entry idiom rather than inventing a mechanism, and the differential path is inert on machines without type-6 entries. Two durability concerns: the vacuum test's validity rests on a self-chosen 2x-excursion threshold that admits 7 of 26 pairs and that a differently-noisy shot could move, and the efm_index=-1 sentinel is a value that is a legal list index everywhere it is used, so the adapter's declaration path can silently overwrite last loop. The promotion coupling (staged map and 53-loop stores must travel as one unit) is real and is recorded as a follow-on rather than left implicit.
justifications.evidence: strong and independently reproduced: both gates re-run green at the reviewed head from a scratch extraction (42 passed, 39 passed), the negative control re-derived and shown to be red with the same two ids, the vacuum test shown not to be vacuous (26 differential rows present, 7 scored, all seven below -0.9, zero under a reversed subtraction), the live bundle shown to still carry 27 loops, and the whole-tree ruff gate green. Docked because the landing fragment states a count its own gate does not produce ('eight pairs (loops 19..26)' against the measured seven, loops 19..25), and because the manifest's baseline_suite is not-run, so the record carries no suite-derived delta.
justifications.fit: the change is exactly the shape the plan calls for and nothing wider: no transform-engine edit, no absent-entry tolerance, no catalog section, no retargeting of the signal-map loop rules (correctly left to jtmm-differential-loop-rules). It stops at the boundary the plan draws for it.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node implements the whole of what section 6 assigns it: the two-index carrier on SensorMapping, the type-6 branch in the adapter that claims no geometry slot, the per-entry map expansion over the type-1 entries, and the second-minus-first rewrite in read_geometry_table's operator for all three Green's blocks, with MAST returned unchanged by construction. The differential convention is right: DD index d maps to slot d-1 and the operator computes second_row minus first_row, which is DD loop(second) - loop(first). Full marks for the delivered behaviour; docked a point only because the shipped map half reads as a per-store split that required the coordinator's decision rather than being expressible from the plan text alone.
justifications.reuse: no duplicated machinery: the map reuses the per-entry struct_array_entry selection already used for PF and TF coils, the operator reuses the existing matrix assembly and rewrites rows after it, and the tests reuse the merged build_magnetics and read_geometry_table rather than a parallel fixture. The new test module is larger than the source change it guards, which is proportionate to a physics-adjacent identity that is easy to get backwards.
justifications.scope_discipline: exemplary. Every tracked change is inside the declared write paths, the external map work is confined to the declared staging directory, the live /work bundle is provably unmodified (27 flux_loop entries, mtime predating the run), no plan or shared index was edited, and the commits carry conventional subjects with bodies and no AI attribution. The node correctly refused the map half it could not express within scope, reported it as NEEDS-HELP with a measured engine probe, and resumed under the coordinator's option-1 ruling rather than editing the transform engine.
